Let the points be  
\[
P_1=(x_1,y_1),\quad P_2=(x_2,y_2),\quad P_3=(x_3,y_3).
\]
The given equations say
\[
P_1P_2=3,\quad P_1P_3=4,\quad P_2P_3=5.
\]
Thus the triangle has side lengths \(3,4,5\), so it is a right triangle with legs \(3\) and \(4\). Its area is
\[
\frac12\cdot 3\cdot 4=6.
\]

Now,
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
x_1 & y_1 & 1\\
x_2 & y_2 & 1\\
x_3 & y_3 & 1
\end{vmatrix}
\]
is twice the signed area of the triangle with vertices \(P_1,P_2,P_3\). Therefore its absolute value is
\[
2\cdot 6=12.
\]
Hence its square is
\[
12^2=144.
\]

The answer is 144.
